parameters.content:
## 🕵️ Leak Detection & Watermarking
**Every copy traceable → sharing detected → takedown drafted.**

### Setup (about 14 minutes)
1. **⚙️ Config** → `storeName`, `alertEmail`, `legalName`.
2. Call the Production URL with `{action:'stamp', orderId, email, productId}`
   before delivering a file — it returns the marker to embed.
3. Schedule handles detection automatically from download data.
4. Found a leak? POST `{action:'trace', marker:'<found marker>'}` or
   `{action:'takedown', marker, url}`.

### Pairs with A1-01 and A1-02
Stamp at delivery, detect from download behaviour. It reads the counters
A1-02 already writes, so detection costs nothing extra.

### ⚠️ READ THIS FIRST — what is actually possible
**You cannot prevent copying.** Anyone who can open a file can copy it.
Any template claiming to stop piracy is lying to you.

**What you CAN do is make leaks attributable and visible.**

That is genuinely valuable: it changes the economics for organised
resellers, deters casual sharing, and gives you a takedown that names an
actual account instead of guessing.

Aim at the achievable thing and it works. Aim at prevention and you will
waste money on tools that do not deliver it.

### 🔍 What it does NOT do — and why
**No automatic web scanning.**

Doing it properly needs paid search APIs and produces mostly false
positives on generic product names. A nightly job reporting forty
"possible leaks" that are all unrelated pages **gets muted in a week**.

So: you find a leak, this does the work from there — trace, identify,
draft the notice.

Honest scope beats an impressive feature nobody trusts.

### 📊 The behavioural signal
One order downloaded from **40 different IPs** is not a customer on
holiday.

The schedule reads what A1-02 already records — distinct IPs and download
counts per order — so this layer costs you nothing extra.

⚠️ Tune `suspiciousIpCount` to your audience. Corporate buyers behind a
VPN legitimately show several IPs.

nodes.name: ⚙️ Config
nodes.notes: markerSalt must be long, random and never change — old markers stop resolving if it does.

nodes.name: 🛡️ Guard · validate + dedupe
nodes.notes: Validates required fields and drops duplicate deliveries. Safe to re-run.

nodes.name: 🔖 Create the buyer marker
nodes.notes: Returns visible + invisible marks and ready-made metadata fields. Apply both.

nodes.name: 🔎 Trace a found marker
nodes.notes: Resolves a marker to the buyer. Includes what to do next, since most sellers have never done this.

nodes.name: ⚖️ Draft the takedown notice
nodes.notes: Standard DMCA structure, pre-filled. Explicitly not legal advice — review before sending.

nodes.name: ⚙️ Config (detection side)
nodes.notes: ⚠️ Mirror of the main Config. Change one, change both.

nodes.name: 📊 Find sharing patterns
nodes.notes: Reads A1-02's download counters. Zero extra collection cost.

nodes.name: ✍️ Write the leak alert
nodes.notes: States plainly that the signal is worth investigating, not proof.

nodes.name: ✅ Nothing unusual

return [{ json: { scannedAt: new Date().toISOString(), found: 0,
                  note: 'No orders crossed the sharing threshold.' }}];

nodes.notes: Logged so you can tell 'all clear' from 'not running'.

nodes.name: 📒 Leak log
nodes.notes: Append to a Sheet. Repeat offenders show up here.

nodes.notes: Answer fast so the provider does not retry on timeout.
